A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same work despite the revised title. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison: Appendices A–M in v1 and A–W in v2. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic sparse-recovery experiments, AudioSet reconstruction results, regression results on three datasets, and runtime measurements in Section 5 and Appendix L.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds regression datasets, correlated-feature tests, cross-validation, gradient-pursuit experiments, image column subset selection, and complex-signal estimation.

M1.justification: The original criteria and Algorithms 1–4 remain essentially unchanged. However, Appendices S–U introduce Optimal Gradient Pursuit, including a selection criterion accounting for gradient updates and an optional threshold for retaining the current support. Appendix V also introduces matrix-residual selection and trace-based elimination criteria for column subset selection.

E1.justification: Regression coverage expands from three to six datasets, adding House 16H, Prostate.v8.egen, and Spectra. New evaluations include correlated, block-sparse compressed-sensing scenarios, column subset selection on eight grayscale images, and complex line-spectrum estimation with closely spaced frequency components.

E2.justification: The original OMP, CoSaMP, and (A)BESS comparisons are retained. v2 adds Gradient Pursuit comparisons in Figures 11–12 and leverage-score selectors using 128 or 256 singular vectors in Table 3. Table 3 separately reports an optimal rank-K SVD reference bound, rather than treating it as a column-selection algorithm.

E3.justification: New protocols include five-fold prediction evaluation, a p=2000 correlated-feature test with n/p=0.05–0.10 and SNR=5–15, and task-specific CSS and complex-signal metrics. Section 5.2 also changes stated polynomial expansion from the first two regression datasets to the first five, including Superconductivity, although its reported dimension remains 80. This establishes a reporting revision, not that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix P adds robustness tests combining correlated features, low sampling rates, and noise. The brief CoSaMP failure discussion in v1 Appendix M becomes an empirical diagnosis in v2 Appendix Q, comparing pruning with least-squares refinement and plotting residual evolution under strong and weak correlations. Appendix U additionally analyzes gradient-pursuit residual convergence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 500-run recovery/runtime reporting and 100 AudioSet trials with mean and standard deviation. The added runtime comparison uses the same 500-run boxplot practice. No new seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice appears; five-fold prediction averaging introduces an evaluation protocol without reporting fold variability.

E6.justification: Figure 3, Table 1, and Figure 5 retain their original results. v2 adds substantial regression, prediction, robustness, gradient-pursuit, CSS, and complex-signal results. For example, Table 3 reports Barbara K=10 error of 0.1730 for OP-(A)BESS versus 0.2437 for (A)BESS. It also contains exceptions to improvement: Cameraman K=3 gives OP 0.2767 versus OMP 0.2749. These are newly reported comparisons, not gains over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorems 4.10–4.11 on correlated-feature selection and elimination, their proofs and a counterexample in Appendices L–M, and OGP derivations and a residual-convergence theorem in Appendices T–U. Appendix I also revises its support assumption to use the best K-sparse approximation instead of the coefficients restricted to the selected support.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same core claims: optimal feature-entry and feature-exit criteria, enhancement through meta-substitution, preservation of theoretical guarantees and computational complexity, and empirical gains. The added theory and extensions do not revise these central statements.

C2.justification: Appendix N adds substantive interpretations concerning suppression of correlated true features and removal of spurious correlated features. Appendix Q connects CoSaMP failure to pruning without subsequent least-squares refinement. Section 6 newly discusses prohibitive least-squares costs at very high dimensions and the applicability of gradient updates, CSS adaptations, and complex-domain extensions.

D1.justification: v2 adds a MATLAB implementation URL in Section 5 and image-source URLs in Appendix V. It also documents Toeplitz covariance and block-sparse signal construction for the new stress test. These improve access information and experimental documentation; the original algorithm pseudocode is largely retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and brief positioning for Gradient Pursuit, column subset selection/PCA, line-spectrum estimation, and the added datasets. The original positioning relative to greedy subset-selection methods and the independently developed SMP criterion in Remark 3.8 remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and publication information change, acknowledgements are added, and a new Discussion section organizes the extensions. The CoSaMP explanation is expanded and appendix references are updated. Most existing prose, including the abstract, introduction, and conclusion, is retained; much of the expansion consists of new scientific content.

P2.justification: Figure 1's elimination panels are redrawn, and Figure 4 is reorganized from nine panels into eighteen panels covering six datasets. v2 adds correlation heatmaps, failure diagnostics, prediction plots, OGP diagrams and plots, a CSS table, and complex-signal visualizations. The retained runtime Figure 5 is relocated from Appendix L to Appendix O.

improvement.justification: v1's sparse-regression evaluation reported explanatory R2 without held-out prediction tests. v2 adds five-fold prediction evaluation and targeted correlated-feature robustness and failure analyses, substantially strengthening assessment of generalization and the proposed mechanism. It also supports new algorithmic extensions with derivations and experiments and supplies a code URL. The inconsistent preprocessing statement and uneven detail for some new experiments remain limitations, but the gains in validation and explanatory support are substantial.
